OFFER LETTER
Dear {{salutation}} {{name}},
With reference to your application and subsequent interview, we are pleased to offer you the
position of
{{designation}}
in our organization with an
Annual CTC of Rs.
{{annual_ctc}}/-
. Your normal place of work will be at our
{{work_location}}
office.
You will receive a Letter of Appointment upon your acceptance and confirmation. Please
submit the following documents on your date of joining:
1. Copy of educational certificates (10th, 12th, Graduation & Post Graduation)
2. Copy of certificates for any professional courses completed
3. Two recent passport-sized photographs
4. Proof of Date of Birth (e.g., Driving License, Ration Card)
5. Proof of Residence (e.g., Voter ID, Driving License)
6. Copy of PAN Card
7. Copy of Aadhar Card
Kindly confirm your date of joining and submit the signed duplicate copy of this offer letter
along with the resignation acceptance/relieving letter from your current employment. Please
return these documents as an acceptance of this offer.
Thank you and regards,
For Radiant Guard Services Pvt. Ltd.
Authorised Signatory
Date: {{issue_date}}
To,
{{salutation}} {{name}},
{{address}}
Letter of Appointment
We are delighted to offer you employment on a full-time basis in the role of
“{{designation}}”
It is intended
for you to commence your employment
{{joining_date}}.
Please read through this letter carefully and indicate your acceptance of the offer by signing and returning
a copy of this letter.
Commencement of Employment and Probationary Period.
a. Your employment with the Company will commence on
{{joining_date}}
No period of employment
with any previous employer counts towards your period of employment with the Company and your
continuous employment will therefore begin on the Commencement Date.
b. The first six months of your employment shall be a probationary period. The probationary period will
be automatically extended by a further two months unless a written letter of confirmation is issued by
the   company.   During   the   probationary   period,   your   performance   and   suitability   for   continued
employment will be monitored. On successful completion of your probation period, your services will
be confirmed in writing.
Job Title and Duties
a. You will be employed on the terms and conditions in this agreement, in the role of
“{{designation}}”.
Your role and job title may change in accordance with the reasonable business requirements of the
Company.
b. You will carry out such duties as are consistent with your position and as may be assigned to you from
time to time. You may be required to undertake other or additional duties from time to time as
follows:
c. During your employment you must:
i. Devote to your duties the whole of your working time, attention and skills during your normal
working hours and at such times as may be reasonably required for the proper performance of your
duties.
ii. Not undertake any other form of paid employment or engagement without the prior written
approval of the Company.
iii. As an employee in the full-time employment of the Company, you are required to devote your
entire time, attention and effort to the furtherance of the business of the Company and to continually
develop your professional skills in your own and the Company’s mutual interest. You shall not,
during your employment with the Company, directly or indirectly engage yourself in or devote any
time   or   attention   to   any   part-time   employment   or   monetary   position   other   than   that   of   the
Company.
iv. Adhere to the reasonable and lawful directions of the Company and anyone duly authorized by
them.
v. Comply with all the Company’s rules, regulations, policies and procedures (as amended) from time
to time.
vi. Use your best endeavours to promote and protect the interests of the Company, and
vii. To comply with the Radiant Guard Services Code of conduct.
Location
a. Your normal place of work will be the Company’s office in
{{work_location}}
However, your services are
liable to be transferred to any other location of the Company and / or any affiliate / associate member
Company. In case of refusal to accept the transfer, it will be termed as misconduct and management is
bound to take serious action as it is considered as disciplinary issue.
b. You acknowledge that during your employment, you may be required to travel.
c. During any work-related travel you will comply with the terms of travel policy and will take all
reasonable steps to keep all personal and Company property secure.
Hours of Work
a. As a full- time employee you will be required to devote substantially the whole of your time and
attention during the Employer’s ordinary business hours to the performance of your duties under this
agreement.
b. Any work performed beyond normal working hours shall be on a voluntary basis, and no additional
remuneration shall be payable for the same.
Salary and Benefits
a. Your annual CTC will be
Rs. {{annual_ctc}} /-
Salary break up is attached as per Annexure.
b. This salary will be paid monthly.
c. The above-mentioned salary is the total cost to the company and includes all payments made and
benefits provided by the Employer directly or indirectly to or on your behalf, whether as salary or
otherwise.
Official Expenses
a. The company will reimburse you for all reasonable expenses wholly, properly and necessarily incurred
in the course of your employment, subject to such expenses being approved by the Company in
advance. For  the avoidance of doubt, you will not be reimbursed for any expenses incurred when
commuting to your normal place of work, or for daily lunches.
b. You will comply with the terms of any Company expenses policy or practice communicated to you
from time to time, including any financial limits relating to expenses.
Leave
a. Privilege Leave: You are entitled to 15 days of Privilege Leaves for a calendar year after completion
of six months from your date of joining. Any unavailed Privilege Leave balance at the end of the
calendar year will be encashed as per company policy.
b. Paid Holiday: You are entitled to 12 Paid Holidays as per the guidelines of the Company.
8.  Security Deposit
a. The Company maintains a policy of obtaining a refundable, interest-free security deposit equivalent to
one (1) month’s gross salary from employees to secure compliance with employment obligations, return
of Company property and recovery of any lawful dues.
b.  The Employee may, at their option:
i. Deposit the full amount of the security deposit upfront prior to or at the time of joining; or
ii. Authorize   the   Company   to   deduct   the   deposit   amount   from   salary   in   equal   monthly
installments, not exceeding twenty (20) installments, at the rate of five percent (5%) of the
monthly gross salary per month or such lower amount as may be required to comply with
applicable wage laws.
c. The security deposit shall be non-interest bearing and shall not be treated as wages.
d. The security deposit shall be refunded to the Employee at the time of full and final settlement upon
separation from employment, after adjustment of any lawful recoverable dues including notice pay,
advances, loss or damage caused to the Company (after due process) or unreturned Company assets, in
accordance with applicable laws.
9.   Retirement
The retirement age is 58 yrs and no prior notice is necessary.
10.  Resignation Procedure & Notice Period
a. An Employee intending to resign from the services of the Company shall submit a formal resignation
addressed to the Management or Human Resources Department, either in writing (signed hard copy)
or through the Employee’s registered official email ID.
b. A resignation shall not be deemed effective unless and until it is formally acknowledged and accepted
by the Company in writing or via official email communication.
c. Upon written/email acceptance of the resignation by the Company, the Employee shall mandatorily
serve   a   notice   period   of   sixty   (60)   days,   commencing   from   the   date   of   such   acceptance   as
communicated by the Company.
d. During   the   notice   period,   the   Employee   shall   continue   to   discharge   assigned   duties   diligently,
facilitate   smooth   transition   of   client   assignments,   ensure   proper   handover   of   operational
responsibilities & records, comply with all handover & clearance i.e. return of all Company
property & data shall be a precondition to processing the Employee’s Full & Final (F&F) settlement
exit formalities as prescribed by the Company.
e. Failure to serve the full notice period shall entitle the Company to recover salary in lieu of the
unserved portion, subject to applicable labour laws.
f. The above-mentioned procedure shall be construed as fair, reasonable & necessary to protect the
legitimate business interest and thus binds all the employees of the Company.
g. In case of involuntary separation or are terminated, the notice pay and exit terms will be decided on a
case to case basis as per the employment status on the date of the termination or separation. In the
event of separation resulted from actions impacting Company’s interest, Company will be free to
exercise available legal remedy and shall be free to make decisions from the outstanding dues as party
of the separation process.
h. In the event of any termination or separation, Employee shall be required to ensure a proper transition
and handing over of the responsibilities to the satisfaction of the Company.
11.  Absconding / Abandonment of Employment
a.  In the event the Employee remains absent from duty without prior written approval and without
valid intimation for a continuous period of Seven (7) working days or more, such absence shall be
treated as unauthorized absence.
b.   If the Employee fails to provide satisfactory explanation within seven (3) days from the date of issuance
of a written notice sent to the last known address/email of the Employee, the Company shall have the
right to presume that the Employee has voluntarily abandoned the employment.
c.   In such circumstances:
i. The Employee shall be deemed to have voluntarily terminated the employment without serving
the required notice period;
ii. The Company shall be entitled to recover notice pay in lieu of the applicable notice period, along
with any other losses, advances or dues payable by the Employee;
iii. The Company shall have the right to initiate appropriate legal action for recovery of damages,
Company property, confidential information or any other loss caused to the Company;
iv. Full and final settlement shall be processed in accordance with applicable laws after adjustment of
lawful recoverable amounts including notice pay, advances, loans, loss or damage caused to the
Company after due process and the value of Company assets not returned. The Employee shall be
required to return all Company property prior to settlement. Any deductions shall be made in compliance
with applicable labour and wage laws.
The Company shall not be liable for any salary or benefits for the period of unauthorized absence.
12. Workforce Protection, Non-Solicitation & Post-Employment Obligations
a. The Employee acknowledges that during the course of employment with the Company, particularly
in a security services organization operating on an India-wide basis, the Employee shall have access
to   confidential   information,   operational   structures,   deployment   strategies,   client   allocations,
manpower   databases,   wage   structures,   and   workforce   arrangements   which   constitute   valuable
proprietary business interests of the Company.
b. During the term of employment and at all times thereafter, without limitation as to time (though we
understand & acknowledge the Section 27 of the Indian Contracts Act, 1872) the Employee shall not,
directly or indirectly:
c. Solicit, induce, recruit, attempt to recruit, hire, engage, or encourage any existing employee, security
personnel,   contractual   staff,   managerial   employee,   consultant,   or   associate   of   the   Company   to
terminate or alter their engagement with the Company;
d. Assist, advise, or facilitate any third party, competitor, client, vendor, or manpower agency in
recruiting or attempting to recruit any employee or personnel of the Company;
e. Use confidential workforce data, deployment information, salary structures, or internal records for the
purpose of attracting or diverting Company personnel.
f. The Employee agrees that workforce stability is fundamental to the Company’s contractual, statutory,
and   operational   obligations,   and   that   breach   of   this   clause   would   cause   irreparable   harm   not
adequately   compensable   by   damages   alone.   The   Company   shall   therefore   be   entitled   to   seek
appropriate legal remedies, including injunctive relief and recovery of damages, in accordance with
applicable law.
g. This clause is expressly intended to protect legitimate business interests and shall not be construed as
a restraint on the Employee’s right to seek employment or carry-on lawful trade, profession, or
business, except to the limited extent necessary to prevent solicitation or misuse of the Company’s
workforce and confidential information. (though we understand & acknowledge the Section 27 of the
Indian Contracts Act, 1872)
h. The obligations under this clause shall survive resignation, withdrawal, retirement, or termination of
employment for any reason whatsoever.
Company Property, Inventory Custody and Accountability
a. Any laptop, mobile phone, SIM card, access card, vehicle, documents, uniforms, equipment, or any asset
issued to you shall remain Company property.
You shall:
i. Use Company property strictly for official purposes.
ii. Not install unauthorized software or applications.
iii. Not misuse IT systems for unlawful or immoral activities.
iv. Employees assigned with custody, handling, storage, or distribution of Company inventory
shall maintain complete transparency, accurate records, and proper accountability of all
stock items entrusted to them, including but not limited to uniforms, shoes, umbrellas,
torches, metal detectors, lathis, batons, and other operational materials or equipment. The
Employee   shall   ensure   that   all   inventory   issued,   received,   transferred,   distributed,   or
returned is properly recorded in the prescribed format/system of the Company.
v. The Employee shall not misuse, conceal, misappropriate, or unauthorizedly distribute any
Company   inventory   or  stock.   Any   shortage,   discrepancy,   damage,   loss,   or  misuse   of
inventory attributable to negligence, misconduct, or unauthorized actions of the Employee
may result in recovery of the cost of such inventory, disciplinary action, or termination of
employment, as deemed appropriate by the Company.
vi. The Employee shall produce stock records and physical inventory for verification, audit, or
inspection whenever required by the Company.
vii. Non-return of Company property shall entitle the Company to withhold Full & Final
Settlement and initiate legal proceedings.
14. Code of Conduct, Misconduct & Zero Tolerance Policy
a.
Standard of Conduct
The Employee shall maintain the highest standards of integrity, discipline, professionalism, and
lawful conduct at all times during employment. The Employee shall act in good faith and in the best
interests of the Company and shall not engage in any act or omission that may harm the Company’s
reputation, goodwill, operations, clients, employees, or commercial interests.
Violation of this Code shall constitute “Misconduct” and may invite disciplinary action.
b.
Acts Constituting Gross Misconduct
Without   prejudice   to   the   Company’s   right   to   determine   misconduct   based   on   facts   and
circumstances, the following shall constitute Gross Misconduct:
i. Fraud, theft, embezzlement, dishonesty, or misappropriation of Company funds, assets, or
property.
ii. Unauthorized access, disclosure, transmission, copying, retention, or misuse of confidential
or proprietary information.
iii. Data breach, cyber misconduct, tampering with IT systems, password misuse, or violation
of IT security policies under the Information Technology Act, 2000.
iv. Sexual harassment as defined under the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace
(Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013.
v. Physical assault, threats, abusive conduct, intimidation, coercion, or workplace violence.
vi. Bribery, corruption, kickbacks, illegal gratification, or violation of anti-corruption laws.
vii. Conflict of interest, including undisclosed financial or commercial interest in competing or
client businesses.
viii. Client   solicitation,   diversion   of   business,   or   inducing   clients   to   terminate   or   reduce
engagement with the Company.
ix. Poaching, inducing, or attempting to induce employees, contractors, or associates to leave
the Company.
x. Willful insubordination, refusal to follow lawful and reasonable instructions.
xi. Unauthorized absence exceeding three (3) consecutive working days without intimation.
xii. Damage, misuse, unauthorized removal, or retention of Company property, documents, or
devices.
xiii. Falsification of records, attendance manipulation, expense fraud, or submission of forged
documents.
xiv. Criminal conduct, moral turpitude, or conviction by a court of law affecting employment.
xv. Any act causing financial loss, reputational harm, operational disruption, or regulatory
exposure to the Company.
The above list is illustrative and not exhaustive.
c. Disciplinary Process
i. In cases of alleged misconduct, the Company may initiate disciplinary proceedings in
accordance with principles of natural justice and applicable labour laws.
ii. The Company may place the Employee under suspension pending inquiry, where deemed
necessary.
iii. Upon conclusion of disciplinary proceedings, if misconduct is established, the Company
may impose one or more of the following penalties depending on the severity:
 Written warning
 Withholding of increments or benefits (as permissible under law)
 Suspension
 Recovery of financial losses (subject to applicable wage laws)
 Demotion or reassignment
 Termination without notice in cases of Gross Misconduct
 Initiation of civil and/or criminal proceedings
iv. If any dispute, difference or claim arises between the Employee and the Company in
relation to employment, compensation, termination, obligations or interpretation of this
Appointment Letter, the parties shall first attempt to resolve the matter amicably through
internal discussions.
v. In the event the matter remains unresolved, the Company shall be entitled to initiate
appropriate legal proceedings before a competent court of law.
vi. This Appointment Letter shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws
of India and the courts at Pune, Maharashtra shall have exclusive jurisdiction.
d. Zero Tolerance & Summary Termination
a. In cases involving Gross Misconduct including but not limited to fraud, data breach,
sexual   harassment,   theft,   violence,   corruption,   or   acts   causing   serious   financial   or
reputational harm, the Company reserves the right to terminate employment without notice
or salary in lieu thereof, subject to due inquiry wherever legally required.
b. The Company shall further be entitled to:
i. Recover financial losses or damages suffered.
ii. Withhold Full & Final Settlement pending investigation.
iii. Report the matter to law enforcement or regulatory authorities.
iv. Seek injunctive relief or damages before appropriate courts.
Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption
a. The Employee shall comply with all applicable anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws,
rules, and regulations during the course of employment with the Company.
b. The Employee shall not, directly or indirectly, offer, promise, give, solicit, accept, or
authorize   any   bribe,   kickback,   facilitation   payment,   or   any   other   improper   payment,
benefit, or advantage, whether financial or otherwise, to or from any on-roll or deployed
employee, customer, vendor, contractor, government official, or any other third party.
c. The   Employee   shall   not   misuse   Company   funds,   resources,   position,   authority,   or
influence for any unlawful, unethical, or improper purpose, including securing any undue
business or personal advantage.
d. Any violation of this clause shall be treated as serious misconduct and may result in
disciplinary action, including termination of employment, without prejudice to any legal or
statutory action that may be initiated under applicable laws.
Dispute Resolution and Disciplinary Process
. In the event of any misconduct, breach of this Appointment Letter, violation of Company
policies or any act prejudicial to the interests of the Company, the Company shall have the
right to initiate disciplinary proceedings against the Employee in accordance with the
principles of natural justice.
The Company may, depending upon the nature and severity of the matter, follow the below
process:
i. Issue of verbal or written warning;
ii. Conduct of internal inquiry, if deemed necessary by the Company;
iii. Issuance of final written notice and/or disciplinary action including suspension, recovery
of losses, termination of employment or any other action deemed appropriate.
b. If any dispute, difference or claim arises between the Employee and the Company in relation
to employment, compensation, termination, obligations or interpretation of this Appointment
Letter,   the   parties   shall   first   attempt   to   resolve   the   matter   amicably   through   internal
discussions.
c. In   the   event   the   matter   remains   unresolved,   the   Company   shall   be   entitled   to   initiate
appropriate legal proceedings before a competent court of law.
d. This Appointment Letter shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of
India and the courts at Pune, Maharashtra shall have exclusive jurisdiction.
Protection of Company Goodwill & Reputation
The Employee shall not, during or after employment:
i. Make defamatory, disparaging, or false statements against the Company, its directors,
employees, or clients.
ii. Publish or circulate any adverse content on social media or public platforms that may harm
Company goodwill.
iii. Represent the Company without authorization.
iv. Breach of this clause shall invite strict legal action.
18.       Continuing Obligation
The obligations under this Code relating to confidentiality, data protection, goodwill protection, and
non-solicitation shall survive termination of employment
Kindly acknowledge and confirm your acceptance of the terms and conditions mentioned in this
letter.
We have pleasure in welcoming you in our Company and look forward to a long term mutually
beneficial association.
For Radiant Guard Services Pvt Ltd.                      I accept the terms of employment fully
